Evidence

What we hand over, and how we show it

The acceptance criteria we commission against, the records we hand over, the reference lists we use, and the standards we follow.

Criteria

Commissioning and acceptance criteria

What "passed" means for each boundary: pressure, cleanliness, approach, flow balance, isolation sequence. Written before the work, not after.

Read →Records

The turnover package

Ten boundaries, three questions each: was it tested, against what, and where is the record. The binder is structured so an operator, an insurer or an auditor can answer them without us in the room.

Read →Samples

What the records look like

Five templates: a factory acceptance test record, a turnover index, a boundary diagram, a flow-balance record with its conditions and a non-conformance log. Templates only, no project data.

Read →Reference

Ten leak points

Following the coolant from chip to facility. Not a ranking. A checklist that every liquid-cooling team should be able to score their last project against.

Read →Canada

The numbers Canada's principles ask for

Canada's Responsible Data Centre Development Principles ask developers for measured, independently verifiable water, heat and power figures. They do not say who produces them. What we hand over, per site, per year, and who signs.

Read →Community

Standards we follow

The standards and open specifications we follow, and the gap our turnover package addresses, so that the criteria above are not just ours.

Read →

Prefabricated liquid cooling for AI data centres: we plan and design the system, deliver skids, CDUs, ORv3 racks and cooling plant, and test, commission and maintain the liquid loop in the field. Every boundary comes with its evidence.
